newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels reject proposed transition steps.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels reject proposed transition steps.

text.p: Zairean rebels rejected on Friday as "absolute nonsense" transition arrangements proposed by a summit of Central African leaders on Thursday and vowed to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko unless he resigned.
Rebel "foreign minister" Bizima Karaha told Reuters the only acceptable course was for Mobutu to hand over power directly to rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
"The proposal is absolute nonsense to us. We insist as we have always insisted that Mr Mobutu must resign and hand over power directly to 'President' Kabila," Karaha said.

"That is a choice he has. The other choice is for him to wait for our arrival in Kinshasa and we chase him away. We are determined to remove this man from power, and to remove everything that he represents," Karaha added.
Karaha accused the Central African presidents of "playing games and trying to protect Mobutu. But we cannot be fooled."
The leaders, including Mobutu, urged Zaire's parliament to fill the vacant post of speaker -- Mobutu's constitutional successor in the event of his death or incapacity.
